chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it (to the Imam), said:
He (peace be upon him) said: 'The man enters the grave from wherever he wishes, and he does not exit except from the side of his legs.'
And in another report, he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: For every house there is a door, and the door of the grave is from the side of the two legs.'

key_terms.الْقَبْر: The grave, the intermediate realm of burial

ai.seo_question: Where does a person exit from after being buried in the grave?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the physical orientation of the deceased in the grave (*Barzakh*), noting that while entry is unrestricted, exit is exclusively through the feet, a detail often linked to the ritual of *Kafan* (shrouding) and the direction of the face towards the Qibla. Shia scholars interpret this anatomical specificity as a sign of divine order in the intermediate realm, reinforcing the continuity of bodily consciousness after death. The analogy of the house's door underscores the grave as a transitional dwelling with defined boundaries before the final resurrection.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, raising it, said,
‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The man can enter the grave from wherever he so desires to, and he cannot exit except from the side of his legs’.
And in another report, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘For every house there is a door, and the door of the grave is from the side of the two legs’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad in a marfu‘ manner the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One may enter a grave from whatever direction he likes, but should come out from the side where the feet are placed.’”
